newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Friday due to a new issue on the domestic A share market today and listing of two new companies next Monday, traders said.
The issue and listing sucked much liquidity out of the repo market, pushing up interest rates, especially those for early-maturing contracts, they said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 13.00 percent from 11.70 percent.
Turnover was little changed at 7.06 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Shanghai Worldbest Industry Development Co issued A shares today. Shandong Taishan Tourist Ropeway Co and Jiangxi Dongfeng Pharmaceutical Co will list A shares next Monday.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed, with key contracts rising on a technical rebound after having fallen for more than two weeks, traders said.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose to 2.46 million lots from 2.06 million.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, regarded as a barometre of the spot market, edged up to 120.00 yuan from 119.75 after touching a support line on Thursday.

"Some new institutions began to build positions in this key contract because of its low price," one trader said. "The contract still has room to rise in the next few days but room will be limited due to weak market sentiment."
Shanghai T-bill spot market has generally been in a downtrend in the past few weeks due to investor jitters over lower coupons for new T-bills after Beijing cut bank interest rates twice this year.
